subject: Request: non-adaptive learning assurance + subprocessor lifecycle details (Aegis Health)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: non-adaptive learning assurance + subprocessor lifecycle details (Aegis Health)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, want to start the thread to capture the operational evidence Aegis needs to accept a "no adaptive learning" commitment for your pilot. High-level ask from your team: a signed DPA addendum reflecting no adaptive learning for tenant interactions, plus an operational pack that shows how we keep customer inputs ephemeral and prevent model updates from using production prompts.

Questions from my side so we can produce the right artifacts:
- Do you need evidence that subprocessors are limited to specific roles (e.g., monitoring, backups), or full third-party attestations?
- Is KMS key residency required onshore (US only) or does onshore HSM/KMS suffice for the pilot?
- Any procurement constraints on audit windows or retention periods we should align to?

Attached is a short DPA draft that includes the non-adaptive clause we typically propose. I'm looping Ben and David to provide the technical and legal evidence pack.

Next steps proposed:
1) Ben to share an ops checklist and subprocessor inventory snapshot.
2) David to propose DPA language (minimal redline).
3) Schedule a 30-min call with your security/procurement next week to confirm residual asks.

Thanks —
Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

From: Lauren Park <lauren.park@aegishealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: non-adaptive learning assurance + subprocessor lifecycle details (Aegis Health)

Thanks Stephanie. Quick answers and a few follow-ups from procurement and security (looped below as procurement@aegishealth.com).

- Subprocessors: procurement needs a current inventory plus the lifecycle policy (how you onboard/offboard and notify customers). We prefer attestations for any subprocessor with access to PII.
- KMS: for our pilot we require customer-controlled keys that do not leave the US; if Redwood can support onshore KMS binding for our tenant that would be ideal.
- Evidence: we will need a short runbook showing how prompt data is retained/ephemeral, and a sampling of logs (redacted) that prove non-persistent KV retention.

I attached a brief list of DPA/Procurement questions. We can review on a call next week; Thurs or Fri morning PT works for us.

Thanks,
Lauren Park
Security Program Manager, Aegis Health
lauren.park@aegishealth.com

Attachment: aegis-dpa-questions.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: non-adaptive learning assurance + subprocessor lifecycle details (Aegis Health)

Hi all — quick technical summary to address the evidence asks. I'll join the call on Thurs.

What we can provide now:
- Subprocessor inventory (attached CSV) showing roles and minimal access scopes — monitoring, backups, infra ops. No subprocessor has model training access.
- KV/Prompt handling: prompts are handled in an ephemeral in-memory KV cache per session. We persist only token-level telemetry for billing/analytics with immediate aggregation; raw prompts are not written to disk unless explicitly configured for a customer export.
- KMS options: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS and an onshore-only key policy for US residency. For the pilot we can enable an onshore HSM-backed key and configure the tenant such that keys never replicate to other regions.

Operational artifacts we can hand over:
- Subprocessor lifecycle policy (exported from our vendor-management system)
- Short runbook showing ephemeral storage and log redaction steps (link below)
- Example redacted audit logs (sample lines) proving non-persistent KV retention

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/nonadaptive-evidence-pack (contains the runbook + sample logs).

Hope this helps. David, tagging you for the DPA redline and any legal caveats.

-ben

--
Ben Carter

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: non-adaptive learning assurance + subprocessor lifecycle details (Aegis Health)

Lauren / Stephanie —

I've reviewed the draft DPA and Ben's evidence pack. Below are proposed legal points to cover the pilot and reduce back-and-forth:

1) No-adaptive-learning clause (suggested language):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Content to update, improve, or retrain any of Redwood's machine learning models for the duration of the Agreement, except with Customer's prior written consent."

2) Subprocessor lifecycle: include an obligation to provide a current inventory within ten (10) business days of request and to notify of changes 30 days before onboarding (or immediately if critical).

3) KMS: commit to tenant-bound BYOK configuration. Operational note: we need procurement to sign an appendix that limits permitted key-export operations.

4) Evidence: propose a single evidence delivery (redacted logs + runbook) and an annual attestation from Redwood's security team. For audits beyond that, agree to a defined process and cost-sharing if an on-site review is requested.

I'll attach a redline showing the exact clause placement. If Aegis is comfortable we can prepare a DocuSign packet for the DPA + the appendix that binds the KMS configuration.

David
